articleSummary: Ebola virus disease is a severe hemorrhagic fever caused by ebolaviruses; the Zaire ebolavirus is among the most lethal. First identified in 1976 near the Ebola River in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The virus likely originates from fruit bats, with human infection arising from contact with infected animals or direct contact with blood, fluids, contaminated objects, surfaces, or corpses; it is not airborne. Incubation is 2–21 days. Early symptoms include high fever, headache, muscle pain, fatigue, diarrhea, vomiting, rash, and potentially internal and external bleeding, progressing to organ failure if untreated. The devastating 2014–2016 outbreak occurred across Guinea, Liberia and Sierra Leone, killing thousands and stressing health systems, economies, and social trust. Today, vaccines exist for some Ebola types and monoclonal antibodies aid treatment, alongside isolation and intensive care; ring vaccination helps to contain outbreaks. A One Health approach and strengthened emergency preparedness remain essential.

articleSummary: Outbreak of Bundibugyo Ebola virus in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda has over 350 confirmed cases and dozens of deaths; no vaccine approved for Bundibugyo. Oxford researchers Teresa Lambe and Rebecca Makinson are developing a vaccine, with early June 2026 funding from CEPI. Bundibugyo, first identified in 2007 in western Uganda, is a zoonotic filovirus with fruit bats suspected as natural reservoirs. While related to Zaire Ebola, Bundibugyo’s glycoprotein amino acid sequence is about 60% similar, limiting confidence that vaccines targeting Zaire would protect against Bundibugyo. Two vaccines licensed for Zaire exist: Ervebo (single-shot) and Zabdeno/Mvabea (two-shot), both viral-vector vaccines delivering Ebola glycoprotein. The main hurdles are funding and logistics; outbreaks affect relatively few people but have high fatality and occur where healthcare infrastructure is weak, complicating manufacturing, transport, storage, and rapid immunization. articleSummary: Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has reached 710 confirmed cases with 149 deaths as of June 13, 2026. A further 324 patients are in isolation or hospitalized, and 35 have recovered. The government says it continues public health interventions to interrupt transmission, including epidemiological surveillance, patient care, and contact tracing. The World Health Organization notes the outbreak is still rapidly evolving, with cases rising and geographic spread widening. The current fatality rate is around 20%, though the true rate may be higher due to deaths under investigation. Ongoing response emphasizes containment, clinical management, and tracing contacts to curb spread.

articleSummary: Confirmed Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo have risen to 710, with 149 deaths, government data show. A field report documenting 21 new infections in the last 24 hours indicates the total confirmed figure through Friday. WHO warns the eastern outbreak remains active and spreading to new areas. Most cases are concentrated in Ituri province in the northeast, with additional cases in 34 health zones across Ituri, North Kivu, and South Kivu. Olivier Le Bolan, WHO head of the Epidemiology and Analysis Unit for Interventions based in Beni, North Kivu, says new infections are detected almost daily in new health zones, underscoring transmission scale and the need to strengthen surveillance, contact tracing, and testing, especially in North Kivu. Response is hampered by weak health systems and insecurity, but WHO notes DRC has substantial Ebola experience, particularly in the current outbreak areas.

articleHeadline: Malaysia records third-highest dengue caseload in Asean, says Dzulkefly | New Straits Times
articleSummary: Malaysia records 33,367 dengue cases in 2026 as of June 13, up 20.7% from 2025, ranking third in ASEAN behind Indonesia (39,672) and Vietnam (35,986). Dengue deaths rose 43.75% to 23. Laboratory surveillance shows an extreme serotype shift, with DENV-3 now dominant in Malaysia’s infection cycle. In Sabah, 2,866 dengue cases (+50.4% YoY) are reported, with Kota Kinabalu (1,033), Tawau (578), and Sandakan (500) among the districts with the highest transmission; Penampang and Putatan also affected. Despite the rise, Sabah records zero dengue deaths this year. Health authorities will bolster dengue control via the Dengue-Free Community Initiative (KomBeD), incorporating behavioural insights. On malaria, Malaysia has had zero locally transmitted indigenous human cases since 2018; zoonotic Plasmodium knowlesi accounted for 80.55% of malaria cases in 2025 (2,088); 504 human malaria cases were imported/introduced. Sabah is national host this year, highlighting a One Health approach to zoonotic malaria.

articleHeadline: 'Snail fever' scourge worries Libanan, calls for House probe
articleSummary: Schistosomiasis, or 'snail fever,' remains endemic in 28 provinces across Visayas and Mindanao, including Eastern Visayas, Caraga, and Northern Mindanao, affecting subsistence farmers and fisherfolk. The parasite Schistosoma japonicum is transmitted via freshwater contaminated by snails, causing chronic abdominal pain, diarrhea, liver enlargement, anemia, stunted growth in children, reduced physical capacity, and, in severe cases, irreversible organ damage. Minority Leader Nonoy Libanan and Rep. Christopher Gonzales filed House Resolution HR No. 1059 urging a House inquiry into the DOH Schistosomiasis Control and Elimination Program (SCEP) to identify policy and implementation gaps despite ongoing interventions. The DOH program includes annual mass drug administration, snail control, water and sanitation initiatives, surveillance, and education, but transmission persists, partly due to animal reservoirs like carabaos, cattle, and dogs and inter-agency coordination challenges. The inquiry could push for increased funding, intensified MDA, stronger veterinary measures, and expanded community education.

articleSummary: June 14, 2026: A locally acquired dengue fever cluster at Kaohsiung Minsheng Hospital, Kaohsiung City, Taiwan, has six confirmed cases linked to the hospital; no evidence of community spread yet. articleSummary: Ebola virus disease in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has risen to 710 confirmed cases, with 149 deaths, government data show through Friday. A field report documented 21 new infections in the last 24 hours, bringing the total confirmed cases to date. The outbreak is driven by the rare Bundibugyo strain, making it one of the most complex Ebola epidemics in recent years. Transmission is hampered by conflict, insecurity, displacement, mistrust of authorities, and challenges in identifying and isolating contacts. More than 4,000 contacts are under monitoring across three affected provinces, though field teams have reached fewer than half. The situation underscores severe public health response challenges in the conflict-affected region as of 2026-06-14.

articleHeadline: Mittelman: Efforts to contain Ebola offer hope for a viable humanitarian system
articleSummary: Ebola Bundibugyo, circulating across the DRC, Uganda, and South Sudan, remains a cross-border threat. The DRC has recorded 17 Ebola outbreaks since 1976, with only three other known outbreaks of the current Bundibugyo strain; transmission is via bodily fluids, and no vaccine or drug exists. Four challenges impede containment: crumbling infrastructure and scarce isolation wards; political instability and mineral-resource exploitation by outsiders; insufficient international support amid USAID cuts and withdrawal from WHO, plus misaligned travel bans; and cultural burial practices that can spread the virus, though education is underway. Optimism exists: Swahili outlets like Nipashe (May 23, 2026) anticipate a vaccine in six to nine months, with Oxford and Serum Institute of India contributing. The State Department has pledged $112 million. The author urges empowering local communities, balancing IP with access, and funding protective gear for traditional funerals, viewing this as a containment opportunity.

articleSummary: As of 2026-06-14 in Hong Kong, a local H9 avian influenza infection was confirmed in a two-year-old boy with a mild condition. articleHeadline: Inside the race to develop a new Ebola vaccine
articleSummary: June 14, 2026 — With the Ebola outbreak raging in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda, Moderna, IAVI, and the University of Oxford are racing to develop an mRNA vaccine against Bundibugyo virus, a rarer Ebola species. Moderna’s investigational mRNA vaccine, backed by CEPI with up to $50 million, aims for a phase 1 safety trial within months, pending regulatory reviews; CEPI has also pledged up to $60 million to fund three Bundibugyo vaccine candidates, including IAVI’s recombinant vesicular stomatitis virus vector and Oxford’s ChAdOx chimpanzee adenovirus platform manufactured by Serum Institute of India. IAVI has received up to $3.2 million for work needed to prepare a master virus seed stock, a starting material for vaccine manufacturing; Oxford/Serum up to $8.6 million for preclinical testing, vaccine development and manufacturing of clinical-grade doses. Mixing platforms aims to broaden protection beyond the Ebola virus licensed vaccine Ervebo; if early results are positive, late-stage trials could lead to emergency use authorization or licensure.

articleHeadline: Tuberculosis may spread before people realize they are sick, a new study warns
articleSummary: Tuberculosis in eastern China (Jiangsu Province) may spread before symptoms. In four centers, researchers followed >1,000 household contacts and 560 neighbors of TB patients, using QuantiFERON blood tests and tuberculin skin tests. Definitions of symptom-free varied: strict no symptoms (~15%), no cough (~25%), and a looser standard of any cough-free period—placing nearly half as symptom-free under the loosest rule. Regardless, about 25% of contacts tested positive, similar across exposure groups; neighbors without known exposure showed ~14% positivity. Among the strictest cutoffs, contacts of symptom-free patients were 3–4 times more likely than unexposed neighbors to test positive. Findings indicate patients who feel fine can be nearly as infectious at home as overtly ill patients, challenging cough-based screening. Implications: non-symptom-based screening (chest X-ray, broader blood tests) and treating household contacts as exposed with preventive treatment if positive. Published in Nature Communications, 2026-06-14.

articleSummary: SARS-CoV-2 has infected over 700 million people globally and caused about 7 million deaths, while emergent viruses such as mpox, chikungunya, hantavirus, and Ebola highlight repeated spillovers. Mpox, originally confined to Africa, erupted worldwide in 2022–2023 with roughly 100,000 confirmed cases in more than 120 countries; France reported over 4,000 cases. In 2025 France saw unusually high chikungunya activity, with more than 800 autochthonous infections. In May 2026, an Andes hantavirus outbreak was linked to the MV Hondius, and Ebola outbreaks persisted in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Viruses evolve rapidly via mutations, recombination, or reassortment, outpacing bacteria and many parasites; about three-quarters of human-emerging diseases originate in animals (zoonoses). Climate change, population movement, and intensive farming contribute to a “perfect storm,” underscoring the need for preparedness for future pandemics.
notes: 記事は教育的・解説的性質が強く、複数の既知パンデミック（SARS-CoV-2など）や既存アウトブレイク（Ebola in DRC、Mpox global spread 2022-2023、France chikungunya 2025、Andes hantavirus May 2026）を扱う総合論文。DRCではEbolaアウトブレイクが「継続」と言及され、確認地域としてDRCのみverifiedとした。Franceで報告された事象は記事サマリーに記載されているが、Franceは対象国リストに含まれないため含めない。本記事単独ではなく、継続的なシグナル監視が必要。

articleHeadline: Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak continues to affect DRC, Uganda -- Africa CDC
articleSummary: Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak continues to affect the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Uganda. As of June 11, 2026, 708 confirmed cases and 141 deaths (case fatality rate ~19.9%) have been reported. In the DRC, 689 cases and 139 deaths are recorded, with Ituri Province bearing the majority; Uganda has 19 cases and 2 deaths. Across both countries, 25 recoveries and 6,525 contacts identified for follow-up. Thirty-four health-care workers infected (29 in the DRC, 5 in Uganda). Africa CDC’s Advisory and Technical Council urges stronger community engagement, cross-border cooperation, and enhanced frontline response, noting insecurity, population movement, and cross-location transmission. It warns against border closures to avoid disrupting essential services. Priorities include expanding laboratory capacity (molecular diagnostics, rapid tests), improving case investigation, contact tracing, clinical care, infection prevention, and readiness in non-affected areas. One Health and civil-military coordination are emphasized; continental PHEIC designation is recommended.

articleSummary: South Sumatra's Health Office (Dinkes Sumsel) prioritizes screening household members of tuberculosis (TB) patients to curb transmission in Palembang. Head Trisnawarman Saa notes cohabitants face higher exposure to Mycobacterium tuberculosis and should be examined promptly. Prevention hinges on ensuring TB patients receive complete treatment and adhere to the regimen. Screening includes health evaluations and sputum tests for close contacts; if TB is detected, treatment follows standard health-service protocols. Contacts who test negative may receive preventive therapy to reduce progression risk. TB spreads via airborne droplets, with higher risk in poorly ventilated, closed spaces and prolonged close contact with untreated patients. Public health measures include hygiene, healthy living, environmental cleanliness, and masking when sick. Those with a cough lasting more than two weeks should seek care at a puskesmas, clinic, or hospital. Treatment lasts about six months; cure requires three negative sputum results and a favorable chest X-ray.

About 90% of cases occur in Ituri Province in eastern DRC, where war-related displacement of over 1 million people complicates contact tracing. Roads are undeveloped and dense jungle hampers surveillance. Armed conflict and distrust of aid agencies have disrupted Ebola containment efforts. The Bundibugyo virus is described as rare, with no vaccine or treatment available. Monitoring is challenging due to conflict and inaccessibility in affected areas.

articleSummary: Mongolia's Ministry allocates 50 million tugriks (~$14,000) to combat foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) in Khövsgöl aimag, a border region with China, following detection of SAT-1, a strain not previously registered in Mongolia. A potential-infection zone includes 23,311 animals in 165 households; 259,248 cattle in 564 households are under surveillance. A high‑alert regime has been in effect since June 8. The government also plans compensation for animals destroyed under law. In Bayan-Ölgii aimag, quarantine and enhanced controls continue with disinfection of people and vehicles from Ulaanbaatar and neighboring regions; restrictions on weddings and mass gatherings; and a ban on importing livestock, meat, and meat products from at-risk areas; horse events are suspended indefinitely. Mongolia has contracted Russia for 1 million vaccine doses, with the first batch arriving June 17. FMD is a highly contagious viral disease of cloven-hoofed animals; humans may be infected via raw milk products. Vaccination against serotypes A and O occurs twice yearly.

articleHeadline: Ebola cases in eastern Congo climb to 782, deaths reach 181

articleHeadline: Deaths in Brazil raise concerns about India's dengue vaccine, DengiAll
articleSummary: Two deaths in Brazil during its dengue vaccination campaign led to the suspension of Butantan-DV on June 8, prompting scrutiny of India’s forthcoming DengiAll. Both vaccines are live, attenuated, tetravalent dengue vaccines derived from NIH TV003/TV005, intended to protect against DENV-1–4. Antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE) remains a concern: cross-reactive antibodies can block infection at high levels but may enhance disease if those levels wane. In Brazil, 42 vaccine recipients experienced serious side effects; two died and one required intensive care, with severe abdominal pain, vomiting, and bleeding—events not disclosed in published phase 3 data. These cases raise questions about true tetravalency and ADE risk for Butantan-DV and whether DengiAll could face similar issues. Dengvaxia’s history showed serotype-skewed protection and severe adverse events after vaccination. Panacea Biotec’s DengiAll Phase 3 enrolled 10,335 participants, began August 2024, with two-year follow-up; results will inform India’s regulatory review.
notes: ブラジルではButantan-DVワクチン接種後に死亡2件を含む重篤有害事象が報告され、6月8日に接種中断。インドの新規デングワクチンDengiAllも同一プラットフォーム（NIH TV003/TV005由来）のため、規制当局および国際的な医療コミュニティから監視対象となっている。抗体依存性増強（ADE）リスク、ワクチンの真の4価性、過去のDengvaxia有害事象との比較が懸念される。

articleHeadline: Public Urged to Use Mosquito Nets, Practise Hygiene Against Malaria
articleSummary: Malaria prevention urged in Keta Municipality, Volta Region, Ghana, with authorities calling for consistent use of insecticide-treated nets and good personal hygiene to curb transmission. Malaria, caused by Plasmodium parasites and transmitted by female Anopheles mosquitoes, remains a leading cause of illness and death in Africa, disproportionately affecting children under five and pregnant women. Symptoms include high fever with chills, severe headaches, body pains, nausea, vomiting, sweating, and fatigue. Complications include severe anaemia, cerebral malaria with seizures, kidney and liver failure, and low birth weight or premature delivery in pregnancy, with death more likely in young children. Preventive measures: nets, clearing stagnant water, indoor residual spraying, wearing long sleeves during evenings, and prompt medical care. Pregnant women should receive antenatal care and intermittent preventive treatment, plus iron and folic acid. Avoid self-medication to prevent resistance; authorities will intensify campaigns and net distributions during the rainy season.

articleHeadline: Malawi, WHO step up Ebola preparedness
articleSummary: Malawi, with WHO, stepped up Ebola screening and border preparedness as of 15 June 2026. Health ministry and WHO inspectors evaluated screening at Kamuzu International Airport in Lilongwe, with WHO country representative Charles Kuria Njuguna and Health Minister Madalitso Baloyi. WHO will hand over protective equipment and laboratory reagents to enable sample collection and testing if a case arises. Malawi currently reports no Ebola cases; however, Ebola is in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and Uganda. Border surveillance and entry protocols at all ports of entry have been intensified to counter rising risk in affected countries. Malawi has direct flights with Uganda; Uganda and DRC are affected by Bundibugyo virus strain, for which there is no vaccine. WHO notes early symptoms include fever, fatigue, muscle pain, headache, sore throat, and transmission via direct contact with bodily fluids.
notes: 記事はマラウイにおけるエボラ対策強化が主題。DRCとウガンダでの流行は触れられているが、マラウイ国内での実際の患者発生は報告されていない。しかし隣接国からの渡航・国境を経由した病原体導入リスクが明確に存在し、WHOと政府による能動的な準備態勢構築が進行中である点が重要。Bundibugyo virus（ワクチン未開発）の言及もあり、公衆衛生上の脅威度は高い。

articleHeadlineTranslated: Is the Tri-City ready for Ebola?
articleHeadline: Czy Trójmiasto jest gotowe na Ebolę?
articleSummary: By June 15, 2026, Ebola concerns persist globally. In the Democratic Republic of the Congo, 676 confirmed Ebola cases and 136 deaths were reported, with Uganda registering 19 cases as the outbreak spreads. In Poland’s Tri-City region and the Pomeranian Voivodeship, readiness for a patient with suspected hemorrhagic fever remains questioned, as a dedicated isolation facility has not yet materialized. Although Gdynia was repeatedly mentioned as a potential site (public discussions in December 2024 and February 2026), no isolation center exists there. Poland relies on three facilities declared ready to admit high-consequence infectious disease patients, none located in Pomeranian Voivodeship. Ambulances in Słupsk and Gdańsk are equipped with BIO-BAG isolation chambers for transport. A laboratory for dangerous virus research has opened, with authorities continuing to assess imported or exported case implications and regional preparedness.
notes: Bluedot APIが付与した発生地域にはポーランドが含まれているが、サマリー上でのアクティブな感染症イベント発生地は DRC（676 確認症例、136 死亡）およびウガンダ（19 症例）である。ポーランドは患者対応準備状況の報道に過ぎ、実際の発生地ではないため除外。ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めない。DRC のみを対象国として識別。

articleHeadline: ಕಾಂಗೋದಲ್ಲಿ ಎಬೋಲಾ ಮರಣಮೃದಂಗ : 181 ಮಂದಿ ಬಲಿ, ಪ್ರಕರಣಗಳ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆ 782ಕ್ಕೆ ಏರಿಕೆ - Eesanje
articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in Congo has surged to 782 confirmed cases and 181 deaths as of June 15, 2026, with 85 recoveries and a case fatality rate of 23%. The Bundibugyo virus strain is responsible, with no licensed vaccine or treatment available. The outbreak is centered in Ituri province (eastern Congo) and accounts for over 90% of cases; additional cases have been reported in North Kivu and South Kivu near the Uganda border. Contact tracing coverage is about 56%, down from the prior week. Ongoing conflict has displaced ~1 million people in Ituri, complicating surveillance due to rough terrain, long travel times, and population movement across districts. Attacks on health workers and community distrust in hotspots further hinder response efforts. Separately, US officials said Americans exposed to Ebola would be moved to a new 50-bed quarantine facility at Kenya’s Laikipia Airbase, prompting protests and court challenges.
notes: Bluedot APIが付与した発生地域にはLaikipia（ケニア）、Uganda、United States、Republic of Kenyaが含まれているが、記事サマリーの主題はコンゴ東部（イトゥリ州・北キブ州・南キブ州）での流行である。米国関係者がケニアのLaikipia Airbaseの検疫施設に移送される計画は言及されているが、米国やケニアでの実際の感染流行ではなく、対象国リストに含まれない。したがって verified_locations はDRCのみとした。
